description: Save to your durable memory. Memory is a tree of nodes under the areas user, projects, people and topics; each node is one subject and holds blocks, one claim each. The first argument is the node's stem; the flags follow, each flag and its value as separate arguments. To create a node, give a new lowercase-hyphenated stem, an existing node as --parent, and a one-line --description. The stem is the node's own name, not a path: its place in the tree comes from --parent. To update a node, give its stem: each --add TEXT adds a block, each --replace ID=TEXT replaces that block's text (blocks in the order given); --tag replaces the node's tags with the --tag values given (repeat it for several tags); --property KEY=VALUE is merged into its properties; --description replaces its description. Tags cannot be cleared and blocks cannot be deleted. Each block is one plain paragraph: no headings, lists, quotes, code or tables. Link to a node as [[stem]] or to a block as [[stem#^id]]. Block IDs are assigned for you and returned. Example: ["outbox-etiquette", "--parent", "topics", "--description", "How and when to cc people on outbox replies", "--tag", "outbox", "--add", "Cc Priya on urgent replies; she asked for this on 2026-11-02."]. If the command exits with code 75 ("busy" or "changed on disk"), run the same command again.
